designs.note: 1101 the only clear coil with ribbed whorls; rings more than a true ammonite spiral, so titled COILED FOSSIL. Line screened the ribs into blotches, pen kept them. fails [], 25.9 x 30.2 cm.
1201 a round coiled shell with growth marks on pale grey paper (levelled cleanly); not clearly a moon snail, so SEA SNAIL SHELL. 1200's cast shadow printed as a ground band. fails [], 25.8 x 29.5 cm.

All four drew spines, not the bare test; 1303 the only one with a knobbed body, so titled SEA URCHIN. Pale cast shadow lifted to white outside the outline (feathered) before oneink. fails [], 26.0 x 29.5 cm.
Main conch: four leaf or blob shapes, no spire. Backup nautilus: 1451 a whole coiled shell with chambered whorls (not cut open), so CHAMBERED SHELL. fails [], 25.9 x 30.6 cm.

Main kelp: four land-plant sprigs or feathers, no ribbon blades or bladders. Backup bladderwrack: a sprig with a pencil and a ground line, a feather, fused plumes, two ferns; no bladders. Done at minute 83, so no third try. Slot empty.

issues: Fronds and seaweed came out as land plants or feathers both times (the model has no idea of kelp or wrack). Spiral shells came best as round coils; all four delivered in pen, which kept the ribs as engraved lines where line mode blotched them. Mains and backups ran one at a time, no memory trouble.
